title: Impact of Class Size Cap Policy on Reading Scores

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (school and year).
- Rationale: We observe treated and control schools before and after a class size cap policy. DID isolates the average treatment effect on the treated by differencing out time-invariant school factors and common time shocks.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the policy, treated and control schools would have experienced similar trends in reading scores.
  - No anticipation: Schools do not adjust reading outcomes before the policy in expectation of treatment.
  - Stable composition/SUTVA: No spillovers between schools and no systematic changes in student composition correlated with treatment timing beyond fixed effects.
  - Exogenous policy timing with respect to idiosyncratic school-level shocks.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Load/install packages
pkgs <- c("fixest", "readr", "dplyr", "sandwich", "lmtest")
for (p in pkgs) {
  if (!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) install.packages(p)
}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
df <- readr::read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s45_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# 2) Prepare variables
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    unit_id = as.factor(unit_id),
    period_fac = as.factor(period),
    treated = as.integer(treated),
    post = as.integer(post),
    y = as.numeric(y),
    period_num = as.numeric(period)
  )

# Quick data info
cat("Observations:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Unique schools:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", length(unique(df$period_fac)), "\n\n")

# 3) Main DID: TWFE with clustering by school
m_twfe <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period_fac, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
ct_twfe <- coeftable(m_twfe)
beta_twfe <- ct_twfe["treated:post", "Estimate"]
se_twfe   <- ct_twfe["treated:post", "Std. Error"]
p_twfe    <- ct_twfe["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"]

cat("MAIN RESULT (TWFE, clustered by school):\n")
cat(sprintf("DID effect (treated x post) = %.4f SD (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n\n", beta_twfe, se_twfe, p_twfe))

# 4) Hand-check via group means DID
gm <- df %>%
  group_by(treated, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_y = mean(y), .groups = "drop")
m_tp <- gm %>% filter(treated == 1, post == 1) %>% pull(mean_y)
m_t0 <- gm %>% filter(treated == 1, post == 0) %>% pull(mean_y)
m_c1 <- gm %>% filter(treated == 0, post == 1) %>% pull(mean_y)
m_c0 <- gm %>% filter(treated == 0, post == 0) %>% pull(mean_y)
if (length(m_tp) == 1 && length(m_t0) == 1 && length(m_c1) == 1 && length(m_c0) == 1) {
  did_manual <- (m_tp - m_t0) - (m_c1 - m_c0)
  cat("Manual DID (group means):\n")
  cat(sprintf("((T,Post)-(T,Pre)) - ((C,Post)-(C,Pre)) = %.4f SD\n\n", did_manual))
} else {
  cat("Manual DID could not be computed (missing some group-time cells).\n\n")
}

# 5) Robustness A: Simple OLS DID with robust SE (HC1)
m_ols <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treated:post, data = df)
vc_ols <- sandwich::vcovHC(m_ols, type = "HC1")
co_ols <- coef(m_ols)
se_ols <- sqrt(diag(vc_ols))
beta_ols <- co_ols["treated:post"]
se_beta_ols <- se_ols["treated:post"]
t_ols <- beta_ols / se_beta_ols
df_ols <- m_ols$df.residual
p_ols <- 2 * pt(abs(t_ols), df = df_ols, lower.tail = FALSE)
cat("Robustness A (Simple OLS DID, HC1 SE):\n")
cat(sprintf("coef = %.4f SD (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n\n", beta_ols, se_beta_ols, p_ols))

# 6) Robustness B: TWFE with two-way clustering (school and period)
m_twfe_2c <- feols(y ~ treated:post | unit_id + period_fac, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id + period_fac)
ct_twfe_2c <- coeftable(m_twfe_2c)
beta_twfe_2c <- ct_twfe_2c["treated:post", "Estimate"]
se_twfe_2c   <- ct_twfe_2c["treated:post", "Std. Error"]
p_twfe_2c    <- ct_twfe_2c["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("Robustness B (TWFE, two-way clustered SEs):\n")
cat(sprintf("coef = %.4f SD (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n\n", beta_twfe_2c, se_twfe_2c, p_twfe_2c))

# 7) Robustness C: Add differential linear time trend for treated group
m_trend <- feols(y ~ treated:post + treated:period_num | unit_id + period_fac, data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
ct_trend <- coeftable(m_trend)
if ("treated:post" %in% rownames(ct_trend)) {
  beta_trend <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Estimate"]
  se_trend   <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Std. Error"]
  p_trend    <- ct_trend["treated:post", "Pr(>|t|)"]
  cat("Robustness C (TWFE + treated-specific linear trend):\n")
  cat(sprintf("coef on treated x post = %.4f SD (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n\n", beta_trend, se_trend, p_trend))
} else {
  cat("Robustness C could not estimate treated x post (collinearity).\n\n")
}

# 8) Pre-trend check: Only pre-periods, test differential trend
pre <- df %>% filter(post == 0)
if (nrow(pre) > 0 && length(unique(pre$period_fac)) >= 2) {
  m_pretrend <- feols(y ~ treated:period_num | unit_id + period_fac, data = pre, cluster = ~unit_id)
  ct_pre <- coeftable(m_pretrend)
  if ("treated:period_num" %in% rownames(ct_pre)) {
    beta_pre <- ct_pre["treated:period_num", "Estimate"]
    se_pre   <- ct_pre["treated:period_num", "Std. Error"]
    p_pre    <- ct_pre["treated:period_num", "Pr(>|t|)"]
    cat("Pre-trend test (pre-periods only, differential linear trend):\n")
    cat(sprintf("coef on treated x time = %.4f (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n\n", beta_pre, se_pre, p_pre))
  } else {
    cat("Pre-trend test failed to estimate treated x time (collinearity).\n\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Pre-trend test not feasible (insufficient pre-period variation).\n\n")
}

# Final clear numerical result
cat("FINAL ESTIMATE (preferred TWFE with school FE, year FE, clustered by school):\n")
cat(sprintf("Policy effect on reading scores = %.4f SD (SE = %.4f, p = %.4f)\n", beta_twfe, se_twfe, p_twfe))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive. Smaller classes should modestly improve reading achievement.
- Magnitude: Approximately +0.10 to +0.20 standard deviations on average, consistent with prior evidence that class size reductions yield small-to-moderate gains, particularly in early grades. The exact size will depend on the policy’s bite (how much class size actually fell) and baseline class sizes. Robustness checks should show similar estimates and no strong pre-trends.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparative analysis of reading scores before and after the policy in treated and untreated schools.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The class size cap policy resulted in a decrease in reading scores.
